pl-l3d5c3-d1e112.summary: Introduces the question why the Word did not take the person of a man when he assumed a man, which some try to prove he did.

pl-l3d5c3-d1e115.summary: Answers that the Word did not assume a human person because that flesh and soul were not united into a person that he could assume; they were united to each other at the same time they were united to the Word. There are two unions, one of soul to flesh, another of the Word to soul and flesh. He did not take a person composed of them, but united in taking and took in uniting.
claims: The soul and flesh were not a person before the union.
The union of soul and flesh and their union with the Word are distinct but simultaneous.

pl-l3d5c3-d1e118.summary: States an objection: a person is an individual substance of a rational nature (Boethius's definition); the soul is such; so if the Word assumed a soul, he assumed a person.
claims: Objection: the soul is a person by definition.

pl-l3d5c3-d1e124.summary: Answers that the soul is not a person when personally united to something else, only when it exists by itself, as a separated soul, like an angel, is a person. Christ's soul never existed without being joined to something else, so assuming it was not assuming a person.
claims: A soul united to another is not a person.
A separated soul is a person.
Christ's soul never existed on its own.

pl-l3d5c3-d1e128.summary: States another objection: the Word assumed a person because he assumed some man, namely the man Jesus Christ.
claims: Objection: the Word assumed the man Jesus Christ, hence some man.

pl-l3d5c3-d1e131.summary: Supports the objection's premise with Augustine's Exposition of the Creed, which anathematizes anyone who says the man Jesus Christ was not assumed by the Son.
claims: The man Jesus Christ was assumed by the Son.

pl-l3d5c3-d1e143.summary: Adds that Augustine often uses such phrases as 'that man was assumed by the Word' and 'that man was made Christ'.

pl-l3d5c3-d1e152.summary: Adds the Psalm, speaking of the man Christ: blessed is he whom you have chosen and assumed (Ps 64:5).

pl-l3d5c3-d1e158.summary: States the inference from these texts: some man was assumed by the Word, and so a person by a person.
claims: Objection: a person was assumed by a person.

pl-l3d5c3-d1e161.summary: Answers that since it is wicked to say or think this, such phrases must be read soundly: 'the man Christ', 'that man', or 'some man' is said to be assumed or united to the Word not because a human person was assumed, but because the soul and flesh in which the person of God and man subsists were assumed. In such phrases one should look to the human nature, not a person.
claims: Phrases about the assumed man refer to the human nature, not a person.

pl-l3d5c3-d1e165.summary: Concludes that when asked, without an authority, whether some man was assumed or united to the Word, one should not answer without distinction, since the question is ambiguous: if it is about a human person, no; if about human nature, yes.
claims: Whether a man was assumed requires distinction: of person, no; of nature, yes.

pl-l3d5c3.summary: Explains why the Word did not assume a human person: the soul and flesh were not already united into a person when assumed, but were united to each other in the same moment they were united to the Word, by a different union. Against the objection that the soul is a rational individual substance and thus a person, the soul is a person only when it exists by itself, not when united to something else, and Christ's soul never existed alone. Against the objection that the Word assumed 'a man', since Scripture and Augustine say the man Jesus Christ was assumed, such phrases refer to the human nature in which the person subsists, not to a human person. So the question whether 'some man' was assumed needs a distinction: of the person, no; of the nature, yes.
claims: The Word did not assume a human person.
Christ's soul and flesh were united to each other and to the Word at once.
A separated soul is a person; a soul united to another is not.
'The man was assumed' refers to the nature, not a person.
